section.title: Purpose
section.text: N-17 is where an LLM turns one anchor of this spec book into a set of small tickets as data. It replaces the architect as the hub for every cut, which the owner halted for overload on 2026-10-14T00:38Z (rebuild/investigation/03-DECISIONS.md#18-d16-may-an-llm-decompose-work-into-tickets option A), and it replaces the approval stamp (238 of 238 approvals were overrides, L11 F3) with a validator that runs the acceptance on main before any ticket exists (N-18).

A spec-author never authors a design and never edits the repository: the design is this book (D14), the output is a draft record in the store (D04), and the architect reads nothing until check.sh passes (brief C, Seats). The owner's rule is that tickets are small, one concern each, a few files, a diff a reviewer reads in minutes; when in doubt split (~/.claude/CLAUDE.md design first).

section.title: Input: the spec-author brief inside a seat run
section.text: The dispatch's target is ../../shared/contracts.schema.json#/$defs/target_cr: request (the CR ticket), anchor (a pointer into this book), group, source_request (the ticket.request record the CR was admitted from) and, on a rework, verdict_refs (the validator.refused records). N-13 renders the brief with:
section.field: the section or volume the anchor points to, verbatim at repo_sha, plus its checklist section, because every acceptance must map to a checklist item's proof.
every ticket in the store cut from the same anchor (id, title, status, files), so the draft extends rather than duplicates.

one concern per ticket; files declared and disjoint inside the set, new files listed in new_paths; acceptance commands from the repository root with test_ref, and expected_failure for a test that is red on main until the ticket lands; arch_sensitive where the CPU matters; depends_on by key or id; an owner-surface ticket names its screenshot proof; a go-live ticket is separate from the dark build.
on a rework: the validator.refused records verbatim (failing command, observed exit, classification, stderr tail, or the check that failed).
section.text: The workspace is read-only by ACL, detached at origin/main (N-14).

section.title: Output record: ticket-set.draft
section.text: ticket-set.draft (record.schema.json#/$defs/ticket-set.draft), code 100, on the shared committed envelope, written by the draft put after a done seat.result: set_id (equals run_id), run_id, cut_request, source_request, anchor, group, attempt, lease, repo_sha, author_session_id, tickets, rationale, verdict_refs on a rework. Operation key N-17/ticket-set.draft/RUN_ID/r1. A draft is never a ticket: ids are minted by N-18 on acceptance.

A blocked output (anchor contradictory, fully ticketed, needs a ruling, anchor not found) is seat.result 423 seat_blocked from N-15; a needs-a-ruling block carries a proposed card N-28 can post as is.

section.title: Mechanism: the brief, the run, the draft put by code
section.mermaid: flowchart LR A[dispatch target_cr: request, anchor, group, source_request] --> B[N-13 brief] B --> R[seat run, read-only slot] R --> O{structured output} O -- tickets --> P[draft put in the service: shape and claim checks, ticket-set.draft 100] O -- blocked --> X[seat.result 423 from N-15] P --> V[N-18 validator]
section.step: The run: the spec-author reads the anchor, its checklist and the code it names, and writes tickets as data. Write and Edit are denied and its slot is read-only by ACL; its Bash is read-only. It runs no acceptance command: N-18 does, on main.

The draft put (scheduler/internal/closeout/specauthor.go), in the service as N-17, level-triggered on run entities in result_committed with a done spec-author seat.result: validate the structured output again, refuse a draft whose new_paths are not covered by its files or whose role is not worker (phase.failed step draft.put, failure_kind output_rejected), then one Commit with key N-17/ticket-set.draft/RUN_ID/r1 under the spec lease: the ticket-set.draft record, Lease.Release, run:RUN_ID to closed_out with phase_record_ref. No mint, no file, no pull request.
N-18 starts on the committed draft (level-triggered). The spec-author is gone by then.
section.text: Model and limits come from roles/spec-author.json through the bundle (N-13); the deadline and stall bound are run.deadline_seconds.spec-author and stall.seconds.spec-author (../../shared/contracts.xml#timing).

section.title: The ticket as data: what every drafted ticket declares
section.field: t1..tn inside the set; the validator mints the id.
the full title; the PR title will be "id - title".
the node id and anchor the ticket builds (target_node, not node, which is an envelope field).
declared paths or globs, at most seats.json ticket_max_files; new_paths lists files the ticket creates, each covered by a files pattern, so N-18 admits a path that does not yet exist on main.
record kinds from the node's record.schema.json.

per command: runs_in (host or pod), expect_exit after the change, proves (a checklist item), test_ref, and either regression_guard (green on main and stays green) or expected_failure {exit, match} (red on main for the reason the ticket fixes); arch_sensitive true sends it to the arm64 pod path as well (N-18).
keys inside the set or ticket ids outside; acyclic.
always worker: a change to specs or this book is a worker ticket whose files are those volumes.
as before; size bounds the review.
section.text: Schema: record.schema.json#/$defs/draft_ticket and #/$defs/acceptance; the accepted shape is ../N-18/record.schema.json#/$defs/ticket.

section.title: How it starts without an agent typing
section.text: A spec-author run starts from a dispatch N-07 grants on a CR ticket in ready (../../shared/contracts.xml#dispatch), which N-03 created from a ticket.request (writers: N-10 a fix for a held main, N-30 a cut message, N-49 a land row, N-50 the archive ticket). A rework is N-11's attempt n plus 1 on the same CR after validator.refused (failure_kind output_rejected). The run is an N-15 unit; the brief is its argument. No architect cuts, approves or types.

section.title: Every wait, its timeout and its fallback

wait.timeout: the unit's RuntimeMaxSec and N-12's stall bound for spec-author (../../shared/contracts.xml#timing)

wait.fallback: phase.failed step draft.put; N-11 charges once

wait.timeout: none: not waited on by this node; the seat is gone

section.title: Retries up to 3, then recover and report
section.text: A validator.refused is a failure with failure_kind output_rejected; N-11 dispatches attempt n plus 1 on the same CR with verdict_refs and a fresh session; after attempt 3 the CR is dead and N-28 posts one card with the three refusals. A blocked run retries the same way; a needs-a-ruling block becomes its card on the first attempt. The draft put retries 3 passes, then phase.failed.

section.title: Many agents at once
section.text: Many spec-authors run at once, one per CR; none writes a file. Each draft is its own record keyed by its run.

Two drafts for one CR (a rework overlapping a late first run): both commit; N-18 accepts at most one set per CR by its accept key N-18/ticket-set.accept/SET_ID and the ticket_sets row precondition (../N-18/spec.xml#many-agents).
Drafts from two anchors declare overlapping files: both may be accepted; N-03 serializes their readiness by claims (../../shared/contracts.xml#claims).
The anchor changes on main mid-read: the draft names repo_sha; N-18 refuses an anchor_moved draft and the rework reads the new text.

section.title: Status codes this node emits
section.code: A draft exists. Acts: N-18 only.
The draft put refused the output (output_rejected) or failed 3 passes. Acts: N-11.

section.title: State paths and the cleanup script for each
section.text: This node writes no file: the run directory is N-15's (N-15.runs), the read-only slot is N-14's, and drafts live in the store (table ticket_sets, retention by N-01). Nothing is written into the repository: a cut is not a pull request (D04 option C).

section.title: Permissions
section.text: The spec-author seat (N-13): Read, Grep, Glob, read-only Bash; denied Write, Edit, Agent, Task, git push, gh; a read-only slot by ACL. Model from roles/spec-author.json.
The draft put: principal coq-svc acting as N-17; one Commit per run.

section.title: Checklist with proof

item.proof: probe: a spec-author seat on the fixture anchor returns a draft that validates against record.schema.json, with every ticket's files disjoint, at most 6 files, role worker, and new_paths covered by files

section.item: Tickets as data in the contract shape.

item.proof: host probe: the seat's permission_denials show a refused Write for a trap line, and a touch in its slot fails EACCES
go test ./internal/closeout -run TestDraftPutIdempotent: two passes for one run commit one ticket-set.draft and close the run out once
go test TestDraftCarriesSourceRequest: the draft's cut_request and source_request equal the dispatch target's request and source_request

section.item: N-03 can close the CR by its source request.

item.proof: go test TestExpectedFailureShape: an acceptance with both regression_guard true and expected_failure is refused by the schema

section.item: A command is either a guard or an expected red.

item.proof: go test TestRetryCarriesVerdict (N-13 fixture): attempt 2 after validator.refused renders the refusals verbatim with a fresh session

section.item: A refused cut is re-thought with the verdict attached.

section.title: Monitoring
section.text: Counters: drafts_written, drafts_refused (from N-18, by check and classification), tickets_per_draft histogram, files_per_ticket histogram, spec_author_cost_usd, needs_ruling_cards. The Stats screen (N-40) shows tickets cut per hour and the refusal rate by check; a refusal rate above seats.json draft_refusal_alert (default 0.5 over the last 10 drafts) is an alert on N-41 because the brief template or the anchor is at fault, not the seats.

section.title: Runbook
section.text: See a draft: ctl ticket-set SET_ID prints the draft, its CR, its source request and N-18's verdict.

A CR dead after three refusals: the card names the three checks that failed; the usual fix is the volume (an acceptance that cannot run on main), cut as a worker ticket on rebuild/design through the same path.
Cut a ticket by hand: not a path; the owner's words on a card become a ticket.request (N-29) and a spec-author run drafts it; the validator is never skipped.
